texts.f94a0e22c69b: The primary aim of the GEHA (Genetics of Healthy Ageing) Study is to identify genes involved in healthy ageing and longevity that allow individuals to survive to advanced old age in good cognitive and physical function and without major age related disease. The secondary aims are to : (1) Identify the genes which explain why women live longer than men. (2) Develop mathematical and statistical models capable of combining genetic data with health, lifestyle and social data. (3) Study biomarkers of ageing, particulary those involved in immunosenescence, oxidative stress and other causes of damage to cellular DNA.
